name: answer-me-with-html
description: Use this skill proactively and liberally, without being asked, whenever a one-page visual HTML explainer would help more than plain text (a Chatlo-specific adaptation). You write only a short Markdown draft; the bundled CLI does layout and diagrams. Use it for explanations of how things work or relate (flow, request path, architecture, code or folder structure, state machine, lifecycle, history); comparisons, trade-offs or decisions; diagnosis, review or investigation with causes or findings to rank; answers with a table, list, steps, branches or sections; or when the user says "I don't get it / draw it / explain visually". When in doubt, use it: a page is quick and cheap. Also for explainer videos ("make a video") and for changing its settings. Skip small talk, trivial one-line answers, or when the user asks for plain text. Adapted for Chatlo (iOS, built-in WebKit): preview, web actions and WebM-only (VP8/VP9) export use its built-in browser; no third-party browser is used.

findings.excerpt: Upstream updates through `npx skills update` / `claude plugin update` / `git pull`. **The Chatlo adaptation does not use those channels**: this skill is re-adap
